evals.prompt: I'm writing a blog post explaining scaled dot-product attention. Can you make one interactive isometric figure of a single attention head over the sentence "the cat sat on the mat" (d = 4), the polished kind, as a single HTML file I can open? My blog has a white background. Show the actual Q, K, V and score matrices, not a metaphor.
evals.expected_output: A single standalone HTML file, light theme, with one framed isometric figure of the attention head's own structure: a 6 × 6 score grid of softmax weights (each row summing to 1) with Q, Kᵀ, V and the output drawn as grids of exactly the right shapes (6 × 4, 4 × 6, 6 × 4, 6 × 4), rows and columns aligned along shared index rulers, on a datum plate. Heights come from a small pure model with fixed numbers, and the readout matches it. Choosing a query lights its path; flow is shown by a lit conduit or moving tokens, never arrows, and there are no floating labels. `scripts/lines.mjs` prints `line ends: 0`, and if conduits are used `node build.mjs --audit` ends `audit passed`. 4× close-ups of seams, ticks and conduit ends were taken and read, and the element count was checked against the model.

evals.prompt: make an isometric figure showing how inserting the keys 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 into an empty binary search tree builds it, one insert at a time. dark, premium, lots of small detail, one html file
evals.expected_output: A standalone dark HTML page with node pucks on stepped terraces (one per depth), joined by conduits that land on node rims, built from a pure insert model. Each insert runs as an operation: a token travels from the root along the comparison path and the new node rises from its socket in the right place; exactly 7 nodes and 6 edges at the end. One lit accent marks the active path. Scaffolding (datum, rulers or terraces with ticks, sockets) gives density; no arrows, no floating labels. `line ends: 0` and `audit passed` for the conduits; close-ups were read.

evals.prompt: We need a figure for our docs on hash tables with separate chaining: 8 buckets, insert 12 keys (some collide), then resize to 16 buckets and rehash. Dark theme, standalone HTML, interactive.
evals.expected_output: A standalone dark HTML page where buckets are trays on an index ruler and each key is a token that travels to its bucket and stacks on the chain already there, with true hash values from a pure model so collisions are real; 12 tokens across 8 buckets, then a second row of 16 trays and every token moved by its new hash. The readout shows load factor and longest chain, true to the model. Every element is seated, no arrows or floating labels, `line ends: 0` in both themes if a light build exists, and the token count was checked against the model.

evals.prompt: Show gradient descent on a 2D loss surface for a light-themed course page: a bowl-shaped loss with a narrow valley, a ball taking steps from a fixed start, and a control for the learning rate so students can see it diverge when it's too big. One HTML file.
evals.expected_output: A standalone light HTML page with a seated height field of the true loss (skirts down to a datum, shaded per facet), a ball resting on the surface at each step of a pure gradient-descent model, earlier steps left as small tokens on the facets, and the learning rate as a carriage on a ticked track. Too large a rate visibly overshoots and diverges, and the readout (step, loss, rate) matches the model. Motion is calm and eased, reduced motion jumps to end states, no arrows or floating labels, `line ends: 0`, and phone and close-up captures were read.

evals.prompt: Build a React component (TSX) for our Next.js docs showing a message queue with three consumers: messages are enqueued, delivered to a consumer, acknowledged, and redelivered if a consumer times out. Also give me a static HTML preview to look at now. Dark theme. It should look crafted, not like a boxes-and-arrows diagram.
evals.expected_output: A React TSX component (geometry modules, a server component for the static art, one client component for motion) plus a standalone HTML preview, dark theme. The queue is a track of message cells, consumers are pucks with ports, messages travel as tokens along conduits, acknowledged ones sink into sockets and timed-out ones return to the queue, all driven by one pure model. Painter's order is proved by the audit when conduits are used (`audit passed`), `line ends: 0`, no arrows or floating labels, and close-ups of every port were read.
